headline: CRUDE BACK AT $102; BEANS CRACK, CORN FIRMS
lead: Saudi East-West pipeline offline + Brent at $108 this morning handed corn a tailwind and charged beans a toll: WTI settled $102.38, November beans cracked to $12.95, and the corn-bean spread is the widest it has been since the August WASDE. Input costs just got repriced for fall fieldwork.
teaser: Crude runs on Saudi pipeline news; beans fold on Fed fears while corn holds its ground.

one_number.unit: commodity vessels transiting Hormuz this weekend
one_number.context: Hormuz traffic fell to single digits Saturday and Sunday. That is not a blip; it is a shut strait in practice, and crude is pricing it.

action: New-crop beans at $12.95: a settle at or below $12.85 is the sell signal the Sep 12 brief flagged. Do not wait for $12.70.

sections.title: CORN FIRMS; BEANS CRACK
sections.body: - Nearby corn added to $5.17 while November beans fell to **$12.95**, a split that started with the WASDE last Friday and widened today as a Fed rate-hike story hit the oilseed complex hard.
sections.so_what: Corn and beans are telling two different stories; the WASDE is the dividing line.

sections.title: CRUDE RUNS; FED HIKE LOOMS
sections.body: - WTI settled at $102.38 after Brent hit $108 this morning; the Saudi East-West pipeline shutdown, the latest chapter in the Iran-Hormuz cycle ongoing since July, pulled Hormuz vessel traffic to single digits this weekend.
sections.so_what: Crude is a harvest-cost story right now, not just a geopolitical headline.

sections.title: CATTLE FIRMS; HOGS SLIP
sections.body:
- Feeders ran to **$337.82**, up 1.6%, tracking the corn ease; cash cattle held $218-$223 across regions with live cattle adding 0.8% to $219.68.
- Hogs gave back 2.0% to $81.53 with no fresh news driving it; looks like fund liquidation on a quiet cash week.
sections.so_what: Cattle is the one corner of the board acting like it has a floor.

outside_the_pit.title: Oman Calls for LNG Routes That Bypass Hormuz
outside_the_pit.body: Oman's Energy Minister at Gastech said the Middle East must build LNG export routes around the strait.

watch_list.desc: USDA Crop Progress: corn harvest above 10% keeps harvest pace normal; below 5% adds weather-delay premium.
Fed rate decision: a 25-bps hike is 90% priced; a surprise hold would lift beans off $12.95 fast.
Saudi pipeline and Hormuz vessel counts: single-digit transits sustained above three days reprices diesel for fall fieldwork.

daily_quote.text: We can never have enough of nature.
